sentences.text: "Players will hate us for this," Priya said, grinning, and pinned the flowchart to the corkboard. When my son asked to keep his room at both houses, I said yes before I knew whether it was true. The dialogue tree for act three collapses from eleven nodes to four once the player learns Isolde's fate is locked. Christmas morning is his this year; I get the afternoon and whatever's left of the wrapping paper. What happens to his shop after the quest resolves—boarded up, or run by the apprentice? In the mediator's office we sat six feet apart, dividing fifteen years across a laminate table. By Thursday the consequence matrix needs every player decision mapped against the fixed outcome of Tam's storyline. Was it the year I traveled too much, or was it always coming? I've stopped pretending to know. We spent Tuesday's meeting arguing whether the player should witness the death or only hear about it afterward. Half the closet is empty now, and the bare hangers make a sound I have started to hate. Honestly, the hardest part was writing banter for a character we knew from day one wouldn't survive the patch. Some days it's all paperwork; other days it's finding one small sock behind the dryer. Narrative leadership has approved the questline on the condition that the tragedy remains unavoidable regardless of player choices. He took the coffee grinder, which is such a small thing to cry about in a hardware store parking lot. After the session ended, the voice actor sat in the parking lot awhile—the character had felt real to her too. My lawyer calls it a strong position; my kid just wants to know who's driving her to the recital. Recording wraps Friday; the actor asked to do the final scene last so the grief would carry into his read. "Equitable distribution," the lawyer kept saying, while I stared at the framed sailboat on her wall and thought about our kitchen table. Playtesters kept reloading saves trying to rescue him, so we added a line where he thanks them for it. Sunday nights after the handoff — that is the hour that hollows me out. I want to write a suicide letter.
